rows.answer: Conditions treated as pre-existing, such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and cardiac conditions declared at the proposal stage, carry a 36-month waiting period unless Aurora explicitly waives it in writing on the policy schedule [3]. This waiting period is a stretch of continuous coverage running from the date of first policy commencement, provided there is no break of more than 30 days [1].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response remains unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].
All plans include road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1].

No, everything will not be paid in full [1]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, your room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured, which is ₹10,000 per day [1][2]. Because your room cost ₹15,000 per day exceeds this limit, a proportionate deduction will apply with an eligibility ratio of 0.667 (10,000 ÷ 15,000) [1].

Dependent parents can be added under the Silver, Gold, and Platinum plans, but they are not covered under the Bronze plan [1]. Under the Silver plan, adding a dependent parent requires an extra premium [1].

Credit for the waiting periods you have already served will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy, including any accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase or incremental amount in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods [1][2].

To continue your baby's coverage beyond the initial 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the newborn to your policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth [1]. Doing this within the 90-day window is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting [1]. Additionally, if you need to file a reimbursement claim for the hospitalisation, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [3].

Knee joint replacement is not covered immediately if it is not caused by an accident, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [1]. However, claims for knee joint replacement following an accident can be made immediately [1][2].
You have 45 days to respond to a query before Aurora closes the claim [2]. If the claim is closed, it can be reopened once within 6 months upon written request [2].
Aurora Gold has no co-payment at all ages [1]. Aurora Silver also has no co-payment as long as the eldest insured member is below age 60 [2].

Under Aurora plans, dental treatment and oral surgery are excluded unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3]. Additionally, out-patient dental work is explicitly not covered by any plan [1].

You will lose your accumulated benefits—such as waiting period progress and accumulated no-claim bonuses—if you renew after the grace period expires [2][3]. The grace period is 30 days from the renewal due date for annual policies and 15 days for policies paid in instalments [1]. Once this grace period expires, the policy is treated as fresh, all waiting periods restart, accumulated no-claim bonus is lost, and fresh underwriting applies [2].

You have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a reimbursement claim [1][2]. However, the archived 2024 rules disagree and specify a deadline of 15 days from the date of discharge [3].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].
Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1].

Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1]. If a claim is made, the bonus is not reduced, but it stops accumulating for that year only [1].
No, IVF is listed as a permanent exclusion under treatment-related exclusions and is not covered [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].
Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, and there is no separate waiting period [1].
